ABOUTMohammad Syful Hoque

One capability. Many real-world contexts.

An economist and management-consulting leader: economic, financial, social and environmental cost-benefit analysis, modelling and feasibility studies, with the research, policy and advocacy insight to carry them into decisions.

Since 2008 his assignments have been for and with the Asian Development Bank, the World Bank Group, the European Commission, UNCTAD, JICA and the Gates Foundation, and for Bangladeshi public bodies including the Payra Seaport Authority and Dhaka South City Corporation. The work spans feasibility studies, cost estimates, ENPV/EIRR and sensitivity analysis, financing plans, results frameworks, impact evaluations including randomised trials, and policy research on trade, LDC graduation and green transition.

He is currently Economic and Financial Analysis Specialist on an ADB regional technical assistance for early-warning systems.

PROFILEIn his own account

Economist. Consulting leader. Development practitioner.

The figures below are Syful Hoque’s own statement. The work board documents the assignments in his CV record.

100+government and donor-funded programmes taken part in
20 yearsdesigning, delivering and assessing programmes, South Asia focus
5 yearsEconomist (STC), Office of the Chief Economist for South Asia, World Bank

Syful Hoque combines economic credentials with long experience leading management consulting work — engaging in-house staff, clients and the global development community in meaningful dialogue. His lead services are economic, financial, social and environmental cost-benefit analysis, modelling and feasibility studies.

He has taken part in more than 100 government and international-donor-funded programmes across the public and private sectors, and has spent 20 years designing, delivering and assessing development, policy and intervention programmes with a focus on South Asia.

His assignments have ranged from agriculture to industrial development, from socio-economic problems to vulnerability and inequality, from infrastructure to technology adoption, from public health to public finance, and from investment to trade policy — research-based and programme-based, sometimes as an economist, sometimes as a researcher, sometimes as a development practitioner.

Across them he has worked with full access to government, the international donor community, research institutions and development banks, local implementers, investors and beneficiaries — and has worked directly with investors and national bodies to leverage resources for investment, preparing business, investment and financing plans and models for national institutes, private companies and large nationwide programmes.

WORLD BANKEconomist (STC) · Office of the Chief Economist for South Asia (SARCE) · World Bank

Five years inside the World Bank’s South Asia Chief Economist’s office.

He managed a range of analytical and operational projects and World Bank-commissioned surveys in Bangladesh from scratch — from design and budgeting through research input to implementation, coordination and dissemination.

The role meant balancing competing demands from economists in the Finance, Competitiveness & Innovation (FCI) and Equitable Growth, Finance & Institutions (EFI) Global Practices, alongside ad-hoc research requests from other departments.

What the role involved

  • Hiring and assembling teams — firms and professionals
  • Designing and budgeting surveys and studies
  • Research input and implementation
  • Coordination across Global Practices
  • Dissemination of findings
